display.purpose: Payload type, section numerals, module counts, key letters. Silkscreen, all caps, never below 10 px.

title.purpose: QRENCODER in the top bar, and the page h1 at display scale on the site.

label.purpose: 8–9 px uppercase Barlow 600 at 1.9 px tracking; names sections, keys and measurements.

body.purpose: Typed payload text, field contents and the few sentences of interface copy.

mono.purpose: Composed payloads, hints in empty states, export arithmetic.

components.name: Key, selected
components.description: The chosen value in a key row: error correction, Wi-Fi security, hidden network, appearance. Lime fill, ink text, 2 px ink frame.

components.name: Key, idle
components.description: Unchosen keys sit at 1 px ink on transparent. Never greyed out; the value is still actionable.

components.name: Primary action
components.description: Copy Image: the one filled button. Inverted ink, square, 2 px frame; disabled it loses its fill and turns muted.

components.name: Secondary action
components.description: Save PNG and Reset: transparent, 2 px ink frame, no fill until hover.

components.name: Payload field
components.description: A square-bordered box on the newsprint ground, Barlow 15 px, caret at 1.6 px. Focus is the caret only.

components.name: Section header
components.description: Uppercase 9 px label over a 1 px rule, with a Courier Prime count at the right. The only heading level inside the controls.

components.name: Style chip
components.description: A white plate with a live 48 px sample of the symbol, the style name beneath. Selected chip carries a 3 px accent frame.

components.name: Apparatus measure
components.description: One measurement in the right margin: muted 8 px label over a Silkscreen value, closed by a hairline.

components.name: Template row
components.description: A row of the payload picker: name in Barlow 600, composed format right-aligned in Courier Prime, 40 px tall, hairline between rows.

narrative.overview: QREncoder is a lab plate for a QR symbol: a printed sheet with a measured specimen in the middle, the parameters that produced it along the edge, and nothing else on the page. It borrows technical printing vocabulary — hairlines, crop ticks, tabular figures, silkscreen capitals — and refuses everything that would make it feel like a consumer app. The symbol is the only object allowed to be photographic; everything around it is a rule, a number or a control.
keyCharacteristics: Newsprint ground, near-black ink, one acid-lime accent used as a highlighter.
Three voices with strict jobs: Silkscreen for numbers and names, Barlow for labels, Courier Prime for encoded strings.
1 px hairlines inside a section, 2 px rules around it, no shadows anywhere.
The plate is always white and the modules always dark, in both themes.

rules.name: The Symbol Is Never Themed
rules.body: The plate stays #FFFFFF and the modules stay the chosen ink in light and dark mode. Dark mode changes the chrome only.

rules.name: No White On Lime
rules.body: Text on the accent is always #111110. White on #D8FF3E collapses to roughly 1.4:1 and disappears.

rules.name: Draw, Don't Shadow
rules.body: Depth is expressed with 1 px and 2 px rules, never with elevation, blur or translucency.

rules.name: Numbers Get The Display Face
rules.body: Module counts, export sizes, scale values and key letters are Silkscreen; prose is Barlow.

dos: Do keep the symbol ink-on-white at an integer module scale with the four-module quiet zone intact.
Do put a control's current value next to the control.
Do use the accent as a fill behind a selected key, a 3 px underline, or a 7 px dot.
Do state failures plainly and briefly: CANNOT ENCODE, LOWER THE LEVEL.
donts: Don't use rounded corners, cards, shadows, gradients or Material 3 components in the chrome.
Don't put white text on the lime accent.
Don't leave explanatory prose in the interface.
Don't add a Generate button, a spinner or any confirm step between typing and the symbol.
